title: GIN & GiST Indexes: JSONB, Arrays & Search
description: Index JSONB documents, PostgreSQL arrays, full-text search vectors, and spatial geometries using GIN and GiST.

data.text: Standard B-tree indexes are designed for scalar values with a single key per row. When indexing composite elements (such as JSONB keys, tags in an array, or words in a text document), a single row contains **multiple elements**. **GIN (Generalized Inverted Index)** maps individual elements back to rows, functioning like the index at the back of a textbook.
GIN for Full-Text Search and JSONB

data.title: Indexing Full-Text Search with GIN
data.content: Accelerating text search vectors with GIN.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: GIN indexes are ideal for multi-value columns (JSONB, Arrays, `tsvector`).
GiST indexes excel at geometric shapes, ranges, and nearest-neighbor search (`<->`).
GIN indexes are slower to update but provide blazing-fast containment searches.
